status: Draft: every country design is provisional until the roster redesign (R-21 to R-27) settles tags and realms
note: Grammars per culture and people, family marks, a design record per current roster row (305, debug tags such as Y01 kept until the tag migration), the dynamic-tag derivation and fallback designs, the forbidden register and the build checks. Hex values are the design tinctures; the palette-fit check measures generated images against them.

lines.indented: an indented line of small even teeth
lines.stepped: a stepped line like a short stair (grady)
lines.nebuly: a cloud-like interlocking line (nebuly), like a cord pulled through loops
lines.engrailed: an engrailed line of small inward scallops
lines.invected: an invected line of small outward scallops
lines.rayonny: a rayonny line of alternating straight and flame-shaped rays
lines.raguly: a raguly line of lopped-branch stubs
lines.dovetailed: a dovetailed line of joiner's mortises
lines.potenty: a potenty line of T-shaped notches
lines.bevilled: a bevilled line with a single sharp offset step
lines.double_arched: two low arches side by side
lines.dancetty: a dancetty line of three large zigzag peaks
lines.urdy: an urdy line of pointed stakes
lines.rooted: a rooted line from which short root-strands hang
lines.rent: a rent line, jagged like torn hide
lines.fracted: a fracted line, broken and offset halfway along
lines.escartelly: an escartelly line with one square notch

divisions.base: a field of {0} with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of {1} edged by {line}

tincture_rule: A tincture is a metal when its relative luminance exceeds 0.30, otherwise a colour. Charges sit metal on colour or colour on metal (luminance ratio at least 2.2), or are fimbriated.

ainic_men.name: Ainic men
ainic_men.mark_text: Aen's label: a narrow bar across the upper field with three short square pendants, in a metal of the culture
ainic_men.meaning: The label is the medieval mark of a son of the house. Realms of Ainic speech and stock bear it because their first crowns were among the kingdoms Aen joined, and the Reckoning of Lines counts their founding houses among the descendants of his sons (proposed reading). Aenor itself bears none: the crown of Aen's own realm needs no difference. A theocracy bears none, because a faith claims no line.

boreal_men.name: Boreal men
boreal_men.mark_text: every line of partition is indented: small even teeth
boreal_men.meaning: The indented line is the toothed north-western shore that the Aenoran charts met already peopled; Gunwaithic, Coldic and Tritonic realms all draw it, which is how a Triton chart-house and a Cold Lands clan show they share a stock older than the charts.

eastern_men.name: Eastern men
eastern_men.mark_text: every line of partition is stepped like a temple stair (grady); never crenellated
eastern_men.meaning: The stepped line is the stair: the temple stairs above the flood-line, the terraced roads of the caravans and the wells cut in steps. Noric, Stabilic and Alerhic realms all draw it.

orran_men.name: Orran men
orran_men.mark_text: every line is nebuly, like a cord drawn through loops
orran_men.meaning: The nebuly line is the cord of the Old Knots, the oldest custom of men in Aoaz, kept by the speech of the beaten kingdoms.

yonic_men.name: Southern islanders
yonic_men.meaning: The wavy line is the reef's surf, counted wave by wave in the Wave-Tally.

sun_patronage.name: Men under Sunhot patronage
sun_patronage.mark_text: a chief whose lower edge is rayonny, in sun yellow
sun_patronage.meaning: Men who serve the Sunhot sanctuaries carry the patrons' rayonny edge only on a chief: the sanctuary stands over the guest-town, it is not its kin.

sylvan_elves.name: Sylvan elves
sylvan_elves.mark_text: every line is engrailed, and elven silver appears in every achievement
sylvan_elves.meaning: The engrailed line is the edge of a leaf; silver is the Kindred Song. The five realms of the Magical Lands share both, so a hill hall and a lake court are known as kin at a glance.

galic_elves.name: Gala elves
galic_elves.meaning: The invected line is the rim of the Mirror of First Rain. It is deliberately not the Sunhot rayonny line: the kinship of Gala and the Sunhot realms is open, and the arms must not answer it.

sunhot_elves.name: Sunhot elves
sunhot_elves.mark_text: every line is rayonny; a sun disc appears in at most one achievement of each culture
sunhot_elves.meaning: The rayonny line is noon light on a sanctuary threshold. It carries the Sunhot identity so that the charges are free to show what each sanctuary keeps, instead of a sun on every banner.

orcish.name: Orcs
orcish.mark_text: every line is raguly, like a lopped branch
orcish.meaning: The raguly line is the hewn stake of the holds' palisades and the challenge ring; every hold draws it, which says the holds are kin without saying they obey one master.

goblin.name: Goblins
goblin.mark_text: every line is potenty, like tunnel mouths
goblin.meaning: The potenty line is a warren seen in section: tunnel, chamber, tunnel.

isolate.name: Peoples without kin
isolate.mark_text: each people keeps its own line (see the people grammar)
isolate.meaning: Trolls, giants, yeti, ents, the dead and the Netherborn share no line with anyone: their arms answer only their own people.

peoples.name: Men
peoples.line: by family (Ainic straight with the label, Boreal indented, Eastern stepped, Orran nebuly, Yonic wavy)
peoples.ornament: Plain edges; crowns drawn as circlets of the culture; beasts walk or stand, never rampant in a lion-of-a-national-arms pose.
peoples.rank: Monarchies wear the culture crown over the primary charge; councils and leagues wear none; subjects take their overlord's mark.
peoples.kinship: Through the five family lines; mixed realms borrow one tincture or one secondary charge of their second culture.

peoples.name: Elves (Great Folk)
peoples.ornament: Silver in every achievement; long, drawn-out charges; no crown of points, only a leaf circlet for the few hill queens and kings.
peoples.rank: Elected speakers wear an engrailed silver border; a hall-crowned queen or king wears the leaf circlet; leagues of house-towers triple their charge.
peoples.kinship: Sylvan cultures share the engrailed line and silver; Gala keeps its own invected line because its relation to the Sunhot elves is open.

peoples.name: Sunhot elves
peoples.ornament: Tall, narrow charges (the Sunhot stand over three metres); no weapons, because no weapon passes a sanctuary door.
peoples.rank: No Sunhot realm is a kingdom: elders are never called kings. A Speaker's realm is shown by a sanctuary-white field part; the Lands of Light alone may bear the noon-door.
peoples.kinship: The rayonny line. Men under Sunhot patronage carry it on a chief only.

peoples.kinship: The bevilled line keeps them apart from both dwarves (dovetailed) and goblins (potenty) until Q-19 is answered.

peoples.name: Giants

peoples.ornament: One huge charge filling the flag; giants do not draw small things.
peoples.rank: A High Chief or Frost-King is shown by the seat or the cairn itself, not by a crown.
peoples.kinship: The single arch is shared by every giant realm (the cairn seen from afar).

peoples.name: Orcs

peoples.rank: A Warking wears a crown of tusks; a hold-chief none; a Free Moot shows its ring.
peoples.kinship: Raguly line shared with ogres; goblins keep their own potenty line.

peoples.name: Trolls

peoples.rank: The oldest unbeaten troll is shown by the boulder being the largest charge; no crowns (Q-21 on Smash).
peoples.kinship: None declared; ogres resemble trolls in look but are drawn with the orcish line.

peoples.kinship: None declared; the escartelly line is theirs alone.

peoples.name: Yeti
peoples.ornament: Three big peaks; sound is drawn as a cave answering, never as radiating arcs.
peoples.rank: The clan follows the one whose song carries furthest: no crowns, no seats.
peoples.kinship: Old pacts with the ice clans and Titanos are shown by sharing the snow white tincture, not a line.

peoples.name: Ents
peoples.ornament: Every tree is shown with its roots.
peoples.rank: The Eldest speaks last: no crown; a forest domain is shown by the rooted line.
peoples.kinship: The men at the forest edge may add one tincture or charge of their own culture as secondary. Coniferons (Q-18) would share the rooted line if they are kin.

peoples.name: The dead
peoples.status: culture entries exist (grave_hosts, zols_dead); the relation between the two realms is open
peoples.ornament: No beasts, no plants, no persons. Volgan's realm shows a gate; Zol's Mistake shows only its leader's sigil.
peoples.rank: Sworn realms of Volgan carry a grave black base; nothing in any dead realm's arms states who rules for Zol.
peoples.kinship: None: the two realms of the dead share no device, because their relation is open.

peoples.name: Demons
peoples.status: culture entry exists (netherborn); Afrit's demons are never shown
peoples.ornament: Original sigils only: no pentagram, no inverted cross, no goat's head in a star (Q-24).
peoples.rank: A lord or queen of a pact-realm shows its pact-charge; sworn realms take Volgan's grave base.
peoples.kinship: The rent line; devils use the fracted line and are never confused with demons.

peoples.ornament: The fracted line breaks every partition: a service broken.
peoples.rank: Devils serving Volgan bear the grave black base; free devils bear nothing over the broken collar. The lava revival rite is not shown until Q-07.
peoples.kinship: None with demons (demons are corrupted angels; devils corrupted Lesser Spirits).

primary_charge.meaning: the horn of the watch-posts held by a family from birth

secondary_charge.name: a great cairn

countries.meaning: Hilofrim sounds the watch-horn above a giants' cairn: men of the watch who live at the foot of the giants' hills and keep the old pact with them.

A straight watch-horn in snowline white, large in the centre. A great cairn in granite, small, beneath it. A plain narrow border of lamp gold.

countries.name: Klungori Guard

primary_charge.name: a crossbow
primary_charge.meaning: the crossbows and pole-arms of the watch

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the charter border: a plain border of lamp gold

countries.meaning: The Klungori Guard bears the crossbow of the watch under a rising peak: a garrison country whose posts pass from parent to eldest child.
countries.blazon: A field of lichen green with a reversed pile (a broad wedge rising from the bottom edge to a point near the top) of range grey edged by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in snowline white. A crossbow in snowline white, on the reversed pile. A plain narrow border of lamp gold.

countries.name: Noleksun

primary_charge.name: a ploughshare
primary_charge.meaning: free farmers who own their land

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the charter border: a plain border of lamp gold

countries.meaning: Noleksun's three ploughshares are its households: a confederacy of free farmers whose Chief Speaker is chosen by every hearth.
countries.blazon: A plain field of field green. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in chalk white. Three of ploughshare, two above one in chalk white, large in the centre. A plain narrow border of lamp gold.

countries.name: Belurithon

primary_charge.name: an ox-yoke
primary_charge.meaning: land divided among sons, worked in common

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the charter border: a plain border of lamp gold

countries.meaning: Belurithon bears the shared ox-yoke: farms divided among sons and still ploughed together.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, march ochre above and field green below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in palisade brown. An ox-yoke in palisade brown, outlined in chalk white, large in the centre. A plain narrow border of lamp gold.

countries.name: Herez

primary_charge.name: a beacon: a fire-basket on a pole
primary_charge.meaning: the beacon towers of the frontier farms

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the charter border: a plain border of lamp gold

countries.meaning: Herez bears the beacon alone: the Marcher-Lord's stone fort on the pass lights the first fire of the southern frontier.
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, chalk white above and palisade brown below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in palisade brown. A beacon: a fire-basket on a pole in beacon red, outlined in chalk white, large in the centre. A plain narrow border of lamp gold.

countries.name: Asgard

primary_charge.name: a lighthouse with a red fire
primary_charge.meaning: the lighthouse-shrines where the tide-houses name their dead

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the oar-crown: a circlet of five oar-blades
the charter border: a plain border of lamp gold

countries.meaning: Asgard bears its lighthouse-shrine under the oar-crown of the queen the great houses choose: the isle names its dead at the flood and Parim's ships steer by its fire.
countries.canon_note: The name Asgard is under owner question Q-11; the arms do not cant on it.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, foam white above and sea grey below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in deep sea. A lighthouse with a red fire in deep sea, outlined in foam white, large in the centre. Above the charge a circlet of five oar-blades in deep sea. A plain narrow border of lamp gold.

countries.name: Lerendor

primary_charge.name: two waves, one above the other
primary_charge.meaning: Lerendor and Lerenwaith under one High Crown

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the ship-crown: a circlet whose points are raised prows

countries.meaning: Lerendor bears two waves under the ship-crown: one High Crown over Lerendor and Lerenwaith, the northern counterweight to Parim.
countries.blazon: A plain field of strait blue. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in salt white. Two waves, one above the other in salt white, large in the centre. Above the charge a circlet whose points are raised ship prows, in salt white.

countries.name: Eekedor

primary_charge.name: a salt cellar
primary_charge.meaning: salt set on the arbitration table binds both parties

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Eekedor bears the salt cellar of the arbitration table, where the Free Crowns bring their feuds and salt shared binds both sides.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, salt white above and strait blue below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in deep strait. A salt cellar in deep strait, outlined in salt white, large in the centre.

countries.name: R'en

primary_charge.name: a gull
primary_charge.meaning: the skerries and the herring grounds

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the ship-crown: a circlet whose points are raised prows

countries.meaning: R'en's gull over deep water is the skerry kingdom of the herring grounds, a crown of the Leren Compact.
countries.blazon: A plain field of deep strait. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in salt white. A gull in salt white, large in the centre. Above the charge a circlet whose points are raised ship prows, in salt white.

countries.name: Tolhon

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the ship-crown: a circlet whose points are raised prows

countries.meaning: Tolhon bears the seal of the hunting skerries, whose sealskin clothes the strait.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, strait blue above and Leren silver below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in salt white. A seal in deep strait, outlined in salt white, large in the centre. Above the charge a circlet whose points are raised ship prows, in salt white.

countries.name: Allegro

primary_charge.name: a high-prowed ship with one square sail

secondary_charge.name: a hawthorn in blossom
secondary_charge.meaning: the hedged fields and the marriage-boughs of crown-sharing weddings

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the ship-crown: a circlet whose points are raised prows

countries.meaning: Allegro's ship with the hawthorn of the inland crowns says it is a Leren harbour married into the Free Crowns of the hills.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, kelp green at the hoist and salt white at the fly, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in salt white. A high-prowed ship with one square sail in deep strait, outlined in salt white, large in the centre. A hawthorn in blossom in clasp gold, small, beneath it. Above the charge a circlet whose points are raised ship prows, in salt white.

countries.name: Keredor-Hellekton

primary_charge.name: a steering oar
primary_charge.meaning: the steersman's right in the strait code

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the ship-crown: a circlet whose points are raised prows

countries.meaning: Keredor-Hellekton, two lordships under one crown, is impaled blue and green with the steering oar across both: one helm for two shores.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, strait blue at the hoist and kelp green at the fly, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in salt white. A steering oar in salt white, large in the centre. Above the charge a circlet whose points are raised ship prows, in salt white.

countries.name: Low-ness Islands

primary_charge.name: a black skerry rock
primary_charge.meaning: the low skerries of the outer coast

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: The Low-ness Islands bear a black skerry above the sea: low rocks of the outer coast governed by their boat-owners.
countries.blazon: A field of salt white with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of strait blue edged by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in deep strait. A black skerry rock in deep strait, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Molot

primary_charge.name: a bull standing
primary_charge.meaning: the strong hand and the cattle-wealth of the hills

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Molot's crowned bull on hearth red is the strong hand of its lords and their cattle-wealth; of all the Free Crowns it leans closest to Lerendor's court.
countries.blazon: A plain field of hearth red. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in fleece white. A bull standing in fleece white, large in the centre. The beast wears a small plain crown of peat black about its neck.

countries.name: Belg

primary_charge.name: a badger
primary_charge.meaning: the hill-fort dug in and stubborn

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Belg's badger is the dug-in hill-fort that has outlasted every feud around it.
countries.blazon: A plain field of fir green. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in fleece white. A badger in fleece white, large in the centre. The beast wears a small plain crown of peat black about its neck.

countries.name: Goran

primary_charge.name: a crane standing
primary_charge.meaning: the marsh lowlands and a careful watch

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Goran's crane stands in the marsh lowlands it rules, watching.
countries.blazon: A plain field of straw gold. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in peat black. A crane standing in peat black, large in the centre. The beast wears a small plain crown of fleece white about its neck.

countries.name: Sensai

primary_charge.name: a bear walking
primary_charge.meaning: the great forest and the oldest crown of the hills

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Sensai, the largest of the Free Crowns, bears the walking bear of the great forest and the oldest crown of the hills.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, fleece white above and fir green below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in peat black. A bear walking in peat black, outlined in fleece white, large in the centre. The beast wears a small plain crown of fleece white about its neck.

countries.name: Gil'dul

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Gil'dul's owl is the patience of a small crown that wins its feuds at Eekedor's table.
countries.blazon: A plain field of peat black. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in fleece white. An owl in straw gold, large in the centre. The beast wears a small plain crown of peat black about its neck.

countries.name: Ashorn

primary_charge.name: an ash tree
primary_charge.meaning: the ash of the moot hill (canting on the name)

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Ashorn bears an ash with its crown in the branches, canting on its name and its moot hill.
countries.blazon: A plain field of hill grey. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in peat black. An ash tree in peat black, large in the centre. A small plain crown of fleece white hangs in the branches.

countries.name: Gul'dur

primary_charge.name: a wolf walking
primary_charge.meaning: the winter raids it endured and returned

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Gul'dur's crowned wolf remembers the winter raids it endured and returned in kind.
countries.canon_note: Name under the owner's other-fiction review (Q-11, Q-14); the arms do not cant on it.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, earth brown above and peat black below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in fleece white. A wolf walking in fleece white, large in the centre. The beast wears a small plain crown of peat black about its neck.

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: The Heodwa Lands bear the rowan planted at every hall door against ill luck.
countries.blazon: A plain field of fleece white. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in peat black. A rowan tree in berry in hearth red, large in the centre. A small plain crown of fleece white hangs in the branches.

countries.name: Nuatax

primary_charge.name: an otter
primary_charge.meaning: the river-fords and the eel weirs

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Nuatax's otter keeps the river-fords and eel weirs of its two valleys.
countries.blazon: A field of fleece white with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of hearth red edged by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in fleece white. An otter in earth brown, large in the field below the chief. The beast wears a small plain crown of fleece white about its neck.

primary_charge.meaning: the open downs and quick riders

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Solenkovi's hare is the open downs and the quick riders of its three states.
countries.blazon: A plain field of earth brown. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in fleece white. A hare in fleece white, large in the centre. The beast wears a small plain crown of peat black about its neck.

countries.name: Stork

primary_charge.name: a stork
primary_charge.meaning: the nesting storks of the hall roofs (canting on the name)

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Stork bears a stork, canting on its name: the birds nest on its hall roofs every spring.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, straw gold above and earth brown below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in peat black. A stork in fleece white, outlined in peat black, large in the centre. The beast wears a small plain crown of peat black about its neck.

countries.name: Cinargo

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Cinargo's lynx is the high wood above a crown that is small and hard to catch.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, hill grey at the hoist and hearth red at the fly, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in peat black. A lynx in straw gold, outlined in peat black, large in the centre. The beast wears a small plain crown of peat black about its neck.

countries.name: The Hold

primary_charge.name: a timber hall on a mound
primary_charge.meaning: the hill-fort that names the realm

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: The Hold bears its own timber hall on a mound, the hill-fort that names it, with the crown hung on the gable.
countries.blazon: A field of hill grey with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of fir green edged by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in peat black. A timber hall on a mound in peat black, large, standing on the base. A small plain crown of fleece white sits above it.

countries.name: Mustnom

primary_charge.name: a ram
primary_charge.meaning: the wool of the hill farms

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Mustnom's ram is the wool of the hill farms that pays its crown.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper fly corner, straw gold above and fir green below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in peat black. A ram in peat black, outlined in fleece white, large in the centre. The beast wears a small plain crown of fleece white about its neck.

countries.name: Ferlinon

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Ferlinon bears a yew: the bow-staves its woods send to every hall of the North.
countries.blazon: A field of earth brown with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of straw gold edged by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in peat black. A yew tree in fleece white, large in the field below the chief. A small plain crown of peat black hangs in the branches.

countries.name: Thowson

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Thowson's birch is the northern birch wood where its crown is chosen.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, peat black above and fir green below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in fleece white. A birch tree in fleece white, large in the centre. A small plain crown of peat black hangs in the branches.

countries.name: Mina

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Mina bears the miner's pick of the hill mines that make it rich among the Free Crowns.
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, fleece white above and hill grey below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in peat black. A miner's pick in peat black, large in the centre. A small plain crown of fleece white sits above it.

countries.name: Mine Din

primary_charge.name: a mole
primary_charge.meaning: the miners of the hill, who work unseen

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Mine Din's mole is its miners, who work unseen under the hill; old heraldry honoured the mole for the same reason.
countries.blazon: A field of fir green with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of peat black edged by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in fleece white. A mole in fleece white, large, standing on the base. The beast wears a small plain crown of peat black about its neck.

countries.name: Oirt

primary_charge.name: a hawthorn in blossom
primary_charge.meaning: the hedged fields and the marriage-boughs of crown-sharing weddings

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Oirt bears the hawthorn of hedged fields and of the marriage-boughs carried at crown-sharing weddings.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, fleece white at the hoist and earth brown at the fly, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in peat black. A hawthorn in blossom in hearth red, outlined in fleece white, large in the centre. A small plain crown of fleece white hangs in the branches.

countries.name: Pertawn

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Pertawn's alder stands in the wet valleys that are its whole kingdom.
countries.blazon: A field of fir green with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of fleece white edged by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in peat black. An alder tree in straw gold, large in the field below the chief. A small plain crown of peat black hangs in the branches.

countries.name: Filit

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Filit's fox is cunning in feud: the smallest crown, and never yet swallowed.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, fir green above and hill grey below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in fleece white. A fox in hearth red, outlined in fleece white, large in the centre. The beast wears a small plain crown of fleece white about its neck.

countries.name: Dondor

primary_charge.name: a bearded axe
primary_charge.meaning: the clan war and the king chosen from the strongest line

secondary_charge.name: a forged bar with ring ends
secondary_charge.meaning: the bar of iron kept at every hearth and passed to the eldest son

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the iron band: a plain iron crown with no points

countries.meaning: Dondor bears the bearded axe over the hearth-iron under its iron band: the hold-land whose king is chosen from the strongest line and who leads the Dark Sea Accord against Goldoroth.

countries.name: Blackton

primary_charge.name: a chain of three links
primary_charge.meaning: the blood-price: a death paid in iron or in blood

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the iron band: a plain iron crown with no points

countries.meaning: Blackton's feud-chain over sea-blue says the Leren sailors who settled the Dark Lands coast took Dondor's blood-law and kept their own sea.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, hold black above and strait blue below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in bone. A chain of three links in bone, large in the centre. Above the charge a plain iron band without points, in bone.

countries.name: Mirolon

primary_charge.name: a heron standing on one leg

secondary_charge.name: a lamp with its flame blown to one side
secondary_charge.meaning: the lamp every tower keeps lit toward the south

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Mirolon, the lake-watch, bears a heron keeping watch over the lamp turned south: the wardens' monthly vigil against an enemy the rest of Aoaz laughed at.
countries.blazon: A plain field of night blue. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in heron white. A heron standing on one leg in heron white, large in the centre. A lamp with its flame blown to one side in beacon gold, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Nan

primary_charge.name: a gaff hook
primary_charge.meaning: the warlord who takes the tolls

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Nan's gaff hook is its warlord's toll on every boat that passes: the one freehold ruled by force.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, tar black above and sand below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in salt white. A gaff hook in salt white, outlined in tar black, large in the centre.

countries.name: Mirodor

primary_charge.name: a flat-bottomed boat
primary_charge.meaning: the coast boats that came back from the north

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Mirodor bears the flat boat of the Mirolonese who fled north and came back to the coast.
countries.blazon: A plain field of sea teal. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in salt white. A flat-bottomed boat in sand, large in the centre.

countries.name: Mencnon

primary_charge.meaning: the salt trade and the salt laid in every grave

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Mencnon bears the salt-pan: its salt is traded along the coast and laid in every grave.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, sand above and sea teal below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in tar black. A salt-pan with heaped salt in tar black, large in the centre.

countries.name: Luminor

primary_charge.meaning: a light kept against the storms (canting on Luminor)

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Luminor bears a storm lantern, canting on its name: a light kept burning against the Dead Lands storms.
countries.blazon: A plain field of tar black. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in salt white. A storm lantern in sand, large in the centre.

countries.name: Bennen

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Bennen's crab is its mud shore and the patience of a people that does not leave.
countries.blazon: A field of salt white with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of sea teal edged by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in tar black. A crab in mud brick, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Gelon

primary_charge.name: a wide straw hat
primary_charge.meaning: the salt-pan workers under the sun

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Gelon bears the salt-worker's straw hat: a freehold of the open pans.
countries.blazon: A plain field of mud brick. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in salt white. A wide straw hat in sand, large in the centre.

countries.name: Olen

primary_charge.meaning: houses built low against the storms

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Olen's low house under a storm-grey chief is the coast's way of building: low, thick and deep against the weather.

countries.name: Dra

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Dra bears the drag net of the inshore fishers who hold the last cove before the storms.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, storm grey at the hoist and sand at the fly, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in salt white. A drag net in tar black, large in the centre.

countries.name: Cursed Lands

primary_charge.name: a single loose knot in a cord, both ends hanging
primary_charge.meaning: names are knots in a cord: a child is tied into her mother's line and the dead are never untied

countries.meaning: The Cursed Lands bear a cord tied in one knot with its ends hanging free: the Veiled keep every name tied into its mother's line, and no register of the Lost has untied them.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, veil grey above and char below, by a cloud-like interlocking line (nebuly), like a cord pulled through loops. A single loose knot in a cord, both ends hanging in undyed wool, large in the centre.

countries.name: Bloody Forest

secondary_charge.name: a beaded cord hanging
secondary_charge.meaning: kinship by tongue with the Veiled

countries.meaning: The Bloody Forest bears a stag's antlers with a beaded cord: the hunting clans of the cord-mothers, kin by tongue to the Veiled and never tamed by Parim.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, redbark at the hoist and deep bark at the fly, by a cloud-like interlocking line (nebuly), like a cord pulled through loops. A stag's antlers (attires) in antler bone, large in the centre. A beaded cord hanging in ochre, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Coldor

primary_charge.name: a fire inside a ring of stones
primary_charge.meaning: the hearth-law: no feud may be carried past a shared fire

marks.text: the winter crown: a white circlet of short icicle points

countries.meaning: Coldor bears the clan fire in its ring of stones under the winter crown: the realm that united the interior by letting every clan relight its hearth from the crown's fire in the Long Dark.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, frost white above and winter blue below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A fire inside a ring of stones in hearth red, outlined in frost white, large in the centre. Above the charge a circlet of short icicle points in hearth red.

countries.name: Horidor

primary_charge.name: a musk ox
primary_charge.meaning: the clan that stands in a ring against the storm

secondary_charge.name: a fire inside a ring of stones
secondary_charge.meaning: the hearth-law: no feud may be carried past a shared fire

countries.meaning: Horidor's musk ox stands like the clan ring against the storm, with Coldor's hearth beneath it: the great clan-realm allied to the Winter Crown.
countries.blazon: A field of snow with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of fjord blue edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A musk ox in soot, large in the field below the chief. A fire inside a ring of stones in berry red, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Holdon
countries.meaning: Holdon's snowy owl is the winter moot that elects its speakers: the clans of Holdon decide together before the Long Dark.
countries.blazon: A field of ice with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of fjord blue edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A snowy owl in soot, large in the field below the chief.

countries.name: Wonderland

secondary_charge.name: a cord tied with three wind-knots
secondary_charge.meaning: the wind-tokens bargained from the Storm Court

countries.meaning: Wonderland bears the hide boat of its summer crossings with the Windwaith wind-cord: a clan that trades along the coast and bargains with the storms.
countries.canon_note: The name is under owner question Q-11; the arms do not cant on it.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, fjord blue above and snow below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A hide boat in hide brown, outlined in snow, large in the centre. A cord tied with three wind-knots in soot, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Celen
countries.meaning: Celen's reindeer is the herding clan that follows the herds to the coast each thaw.
countries.blazon: A plain field of hide brown. A reindeer in snow, large in the centre.

countries.name: Radeon

primary_charge.name: a wolverine
primary_charge.meaning: a small clan that yields to nobody

countries.meaning: Radeon bears the wolverine: a clan that yields to nobody, not Coldor and not Isengard.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, snow at the hoist and ice at the fly, by an indented line of small even teeth. A wolverine in soot, large in the centre.

countries.name: Orewele

primary_charge.name: an elk
primary_charge.meaning: the forest clans of the southern ice

countries.meaning: Orewele's elk is the forest clan of the southern ice.
countries.blazon: A field of snow with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of hide brown edged by an indented line of small even teeth. An elk in fjord blue, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Gaadon
countries.meaning: Gaadon's walrus is the ivory coast and its carvers.
countries.blazon: A plain field of fjord blue. A walrus in bone, large in the centre.

countries.name: Portogalor

primary_charge.name: a white bear
primary_charge.meaning: the coast ice and the seal hunt

countries.meaning: Portogalor bears the white bear of the coast ice and its seal hunt.
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, snow above and soot below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A white bear in ice, outlined in soot, large in the centre.

countries.name: Omar
countries.meaning: Omar's arctic fox is the trapping clan of the inland tundra, rich in winter furs.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, ice above and hide brown below, by an indented line of small even teeth. An arctic fox in snow, outlined in soot, large in the centre.

countries.name: Felkond
countries.meaning: Felkond bears the snow hare of the tundra clans, white on the dark of the Long Dark.
countries.blazon: A plain field of soot. A snow hare in snow, large in the centre.

countries.name: Yeneldmore

primary_charge.name: a raven
primary_charge.meaning: the clan that finds the herds

countries.meaning: Yeneldmore's raven is the clan that finds the herds for others and takes its share.
countries.blazon: A plain field of bone. A raven in soot, large in the centre.

countries.name: Rion
countries.meaning: Rion bears the orca of the sea clans who hunt in packs along the fjords.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper fly corner, fjord blue above and ice below, by an indented line of small even teeth. An orca in soot, outlined in snow, large in the centre.

countries.name: Xison
countries.meaning: Xison's sledge is the winter road over the ice that the clan keeps open.
countries.blazon: A field of hide brown with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of snow edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A sledge in bone, large in the field below the chief.

countries.name: Hendair
countries.meaning: Hendair bears the leaping salmon of its river clans.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, fjord blue at the hoist and hide brown at the fly, by an indented line of small even teeth. A leaping salmon in bone, large in the centre.

countries.name: Agoron
countries.meaning: Agoron's ptarmigan is the high tundra, white in winter and brown in summer.
countries.blazon: A plain field of lichen green. A ptarmigan in snow, large in the centre.

countries.name: Belor
countries.meaning: Belor bears the eider of the down-gatherers on the skerries.
countries.blazon: A field of fjord blue with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of snow edged by an indented line of small even teeth. An eider duck in snow, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Pertolor
countries.meaning: Pertolor's perched gyrfalcon is its falconers, whose birds are a gift fit for the Winter Crown.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, snow above and berry red below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A gyrfalcon perched in soot, outlined in snow, large in the centre.

countries.name: Londor
countries.meaning: Londor bears the two-peaked mountain of the clan that holds the passes into the interior.
countries.blazon: A field of fjord blue with a reversed pile (a broad wedge rising from the bottom edge to a point near the top) of snow edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A mountain of two peaks in soot, on the reversed pile.

countries.name: Naepu
countries.meaning: Naepu's ermine is the fur trade that clothes the halls of Fandanar.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, berry red above and soot below, by an indented line of small even teeth. An ermine in snow, large in the centre.

countries.name: Fearno
countries.meaning: Fearno, the widest of the clan-realms, bears the whale harpoon: its moot rules twenty-five states of coast and ice and feeds them from the sea.
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, ice above and fjord blue below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A harpoon in soot, outlined in snow, large in the centre.

countries.name: Neridor

primary_charge.name: a narwhal
primary_charge.meaning: the far ice and its single-tusked whale

countries.meaning: Neridor bears the narwhal of the far ice.
countries.blazon: A plain field of ice. A narwhal in fjord blue, large in the centre.

countries.name: Poloto

primary_charge.name: a snowshoe
primary_charge.meaning: the long walk of the winter moot

countries.meaning: Poloto's snowshoe is the long walk to the winter moot that it never misses.
countries.blazon: A field of snow with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of lichen green edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A snowshoe in hide brown, large in the field below the chief.

countries.name: Worlond

primary_charge.name: a seal on an ice floe

countries.meaning: Worlond bears the seal on its floe: the floe hunters of the outer coast.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper fly corner, hide brown above and soot below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A seal on an ice floe in bone, large in the centre.

countries.name: Hozoson
countries.meaning: Hozoson's antler comb is its bone-carvers, whose work is traded down the coast.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, soot at the hoist and ice at the fly, by an indented line of small even teeth. An antler comb in bone, outlined in soot, large in the centre.

countries.name: Yeldenne

primary_charge.name: an arch of two whale ribs
primary_charge.meaning: the bone arches of the halls

countries.meaning: Yeldenne bears the whale-rib arch of its hall door: an ordinary northern town of the clans, governed by its moot.
countries.canon_note: L2: an ordinary northern town. Never Glo, a green crystal, a castle keep, a knight, a blue sword or anything of Horos on these arms.
countries.blazon: A plain field of snow. An arch of two whale ribs in soot, large in the centre.

countries.name: Isengard

primary_charge.name: three spears bound in a sheaf
primary_charge.meaning: the oath-companies that hold the realm for the warlord

secondary_charge.name: a storm cloud loosing three bolts
secondary_charge.meaning: the Storm Court: the Black Gallery's bargains with the storms

countries.meaning: Isengard bears the bound spears of its oath-companies under a storm cloud: a warlord's realm held by sworn men and bargains with the storms, rival to the Winter Crown.
countries.canon_note: Name under Q-11. No tower, no hand: both read as another fiction's Isengard.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, forge black above and war red below, by an indented line of small even teeth. Three spears bound in a sheaf in iron grey, large in the centre. A storm cloud loosing three bolts in storm white, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Windwaith

primary_charge.name: a ship under a bellied sail

countries.meaning: Windwaith, the wind-shore, bears a ship under a bellied sail: owned by shares and governed by a Council of Captains who elect their Speaker.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper fly corner, sea teal above and sail white below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A ship under a bellied sail in tar brown, outlined in sail white, large in the centre.

countries.name: Greenle

primary_charge.name: a storm petrel
primary_charge.meaning: the bird that rides the storm

countries.meaning: Greenle's storm petrel rides the gale its captains sail in.
countries.blazon: A plain field of gale blue. A storm petrel in sail white, large in the centre.

countries.name: Gunwaith

primary_charge.name: a ring of standing stones
primary_charge.meaning: the Oath-Ring where kings are acclaimed and oaths bind

marks.text: the torc-crown: the king's crown is an open torc

countries.meaning: Gunwaith bears the Oath-Ring under the torc-crown on the clan pair: its king is acclaimed at the standing stones and bound by the Lawspeaker, while the chiefs keep the real power.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, clan madder at the hoist and clan green at the fly, by an indented line of small even teeth. A ring of standing stones in torc gold, large in the centre. Above the charge an open torc worn as a crown, in torc gold.

countries.name: Varnondor

primary_charge.name: a stag standing
primary_charge.meaning: the hunting clans of the hills

countries.meaning: Varnondor's stag is the hunting clan of the western hills.
countries.blazon: A plain field of clan green. A stag standing in lime white, large in the centre.

countries.name: Werlendor
countries.meaning: Werlendor bears the boar of the old feud-clans, who want the old claims buried with honour.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, lime white above and moor brown below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A boar in clan madder, outlined in lime white, large in the centre.

countries.name: Lambin

primary_charge.name: a round ring-fort seen from above

countries.meaning: Lambin's ring-fort is the hill country of ten states held by ring-forts on every height.
countries.blazon: A plain field of clan madder. A round ring-fort seen from above in lime white, large in the centre.

countries.name: Thenon
countries.meaning: Thenon's running hound is its war-band, hired to every feud in the hills.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, slate blue above and torc gold below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A hound running in clan madder, outlined in lime white, large in the centre.

countries.name: Hky

primary_charge.name: an open torc
primary_charge.meaning: the chief's bond to the clan

countries.meaning: Hky bears the open torc of the chief's bond to the clan.
countries.blazon: A field of moor brown with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of lime white edged by an indented line of small even teeth. An open torc in torc gold, large in the field below the chief.

countries.name: Lothoro

primary_charge.name: a single standing stone
primary_charge.meaning: the Stone of the Grey Ford and the law of the stones

countries.meaning: Lothoro's standing stone is the oath it swore at the Grey Ford and keeps.
countries.blazon: A field of slate blue with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of clan green edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A single standing stone in lime white, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Girdon

primary_charge.name: a stone bridge of three arches

countries.meaning: Girdon's three-arched bridge is its river-court and its bridge-towns: a Warden-Speaker's realm, Gunwaith's rival under the Truce of the Grey Ford.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, river green above and water blue below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A stone bridge of three arches in ford stone, large in the centre.

countries.name: Argo

primary_charge.name: three stepping stones
primary_charge.meaning: the ford kept clear by the wardens

countries.meaning: Argo bears the three stepping stones of the ford its wardens keep clear.
countries.blazon: A plain field of mud brown. Three stepping stones in ford stone, large in the centre.

countries.name: Pernogon

primary_charge.name: an eel
primary_charge.meaning: the river's keeper spirit is fed at the flood

countries.meaning: Pernogon's eel is the river that is fed a loaf at the flood so that it treats the town as a guest.
countries.blazon: A field of dark pool with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of reed gold edged by an indented line of small even teeth. An eel in ford stone, large in the field below the chief.

countries.name: Kradlon
countries.meaning: Kradlon, seat of the great guild-halls, bears the weavers' shuttle on wine and ivory quarters: a council of guilds that answers to its book, not to a crown.
countries.blazon: A field quartered guild wine and ivory, the upper hoist quarter guild wine, by an indented line of small even teeth. A weaver's shuttle in guild gold, outlined in ink black, large in the centre.

countries.name: Corogon
countries.meaning: Corogon bears the clothiers' shears: the second great guild-city, whose Fair of Contracts sets prices for the West.
countries.blazon: A field quartered guild blue and guild gold, the upper hoist quarter guild blue, by an indented line of small even teeth. Cloth shears in ivory, outlined in ink black, large in the centre.

countries.name: Toples
countries.meaning: Toples bears the coopers' barrel of a one-state port that packs the West's trade.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, vermilion at the hoist and ivory at the fly, by an indented line of small even teeth. A barrel in ink black, large in the centre.

countries.name: Sarudon
countries.meaning: Sarudon's candle is the chandlers' town that lights the guild-halls.
countries.blazon: A plain field of guild green. A candle in ivory, large in the centre.

countries.name: Saopon
countries.meaning: Saopon bears the apothecaries' mortar: its physic-gardens supply three states.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, guild gold above and ink black below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A mortar and pestle in vermilion, large in the centre.

countries.name: Sobre
countries.meaning: Sobre's boot is the cordwainers' guild that shoes the companies of Buldor.
countries.blazon: A field of ivory with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of guild wine edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A boot in ink black, large in the field below the chief.

countries.name: Canako
countries.meaning: Canako bears the wool-comb of the combers who prepare the hill wool for Kradlon's looms.
countries.blazon: A plain field of guild wine. A wool comb in ivory, large in the centre.

countries.name: Forbo
countries.meaning: Forbo's bellows are the smiths' guild of a one-state forge town.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, guild blue above and vermilion below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A pair of bellows in ivory, large in the centre.

countries.name: Oslinod
countries.meaning: Oslinod bears the glovers' glove: the town's fine leather is sent to every court.
countries.blazon: A field of ivory with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of guild green edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A glove in guild wine, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Trilino
countries.meaning: Trilino's corded bale is the merchant-adventurers who carry the guilds' goods abroad.
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, ink black above and guild gold below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A corded bale in ivory, outlined in ink black, large in the centre.

countries.name: Buldor

primary_charge.name: a halberd
primary_charge.meaning: the companies' weapon and the Banner-Oath sworn before it

secondary_charge.name: a war drum
secondary_charge.meaning: the Unfurling and the Last Muster

marks.text: a border compony: compony of livery red and buff

countries.meaning: Buldor bears a halberd and drum within a border of livery blocks: the companies' banner-towns, whose Captain-General is elected by the company-lords and who serve Gunwaith and Girdon alike.
countries.blazon: A field of steel blue within a border of livery red edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A halberd in buff, large within the border. A war drum in olive, small, beneath it. The border is compony: alternating blocks of livery red and buff.

countries.name: Adel

primary_charge.name: a chart-rose of sixteen thin points
primary_charge.meaning: the charts the islands sell to Aenor

countries.meaning: Adel bears the sixteen-pointed chart-rose: the senior chart-house of Triton's Islands, whose charts Aenor buys.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, chart paper above and chart teal below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A chart-rose of sixteen thin points in reef coral, outlined in chart paper, large in the centre.

countries.name: Pollos

primary_charge.name: a sounding lead on its line

countries.meaning: Pollos bears the sounding lead of the pilots who have sounded every reef of its single island.
countries.blazon: A plain field of chart teal. A sounding lead on its line in chart paper, large in the centre.

countries.name: Raerby

primary_charge.name: a branching coral
primary_charge.meaning: the reef-spirits that spared the first pilot

countries.meaning: Raerby's branching coral honours the reef-spirits that spared its first pilot.
countries.blazon: A field of chart paper with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of ink edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A branching coral in reef coral, large in the field below the chief.

countries.name: Ziza
countries.meaning: Ziza bears the pilot's lantern of the harbour that guides ships through two islands' channels.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, chart teal above and sand gold below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A pilot's lantern in ink, large in the centre.

countries.name: The Lens

primary_charge.name: a round lens of ground glass

countries.meaning: The Lens bears a round lens of ground glass, canting on its name: the lens-grinders whose glasses read the charts.
countries.blazon: A plain field of ink. A round lens of ground glass in chart paper, large in the centre.

countries.name: Fineger
countries.meaning: Fineger bears a rolled chart from its chart-house archive.
countries.blazon: A field of chart paper with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of reef coral edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A rolled chart in ink, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Tses - The Vestes

primary_charge.name: a ring with a sighting rule across it

countries.meaning: Tses - The Vestes bears the sighting ring of the star-readers who hold its two isles.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, chart teal at the hoist and chart paper at the fly, by an indented line of small even teeth. A ring with a sighting rule across it in ink, large in the centre.

countries.name: Beemste
countries.meaning: Beemste's sand-glass is the watch kept at sea.
countries.blazon: A plain field of sand gold. A sand-glass in ink, large in the centre.

countries.name: Hiohon
countries.meaning: Hiohon bears the buoy that marks its channels.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper fly corner, shallows above and ink below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A buoy in reef coral, large in the centre.

countries.name: Anbei
countries.meaning: Anbei's coil of rope is its rope-walk, which rigs half the island fleets.
countries.blazon: A field of chart teal with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of chart paper edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A coil of rope in sand gold, large in the field below the chief.

countries.name: Seite Islands
countries.meaning: The Seite Islands bear the turtle of their beaches and of the reef-shrines that stand above them.
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, chart paper above and chart teal below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A turtle in ink, large in the centre.

countries.name: Mondeluz
countries.meaning: Mondeluz bears the seahorse of its sheltered lagoon.
countries.blazon: A plain field of reef coral. A seahorse in chart paper, large in the centre.

countries.name: Kile Islands
countries.meaning: The Kile Islands bear the flying fish of the open crossings between them.
countries.blazon: A field of shallows with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of chart teal edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A flying fish in ink, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Hesos
countries.meaning: Hesos's tern is the outer islet it holds alone.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, ink above and shallows below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A tern in chart paper, outlined in ink, large in the centre.

countries.name: Halenor
countries.meaning: Halenor, the largest chart-house realm, bears its stilt chart-house: four states of harbours governed from it.
countries.blazon: A field of chart teal with a reversed pile (a broad wedge rising from the bottom edge to a point near the top) of sand gold edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A chart-house on stilts in ink, on the reversed pile.

countries.name: Urbolon
countries.meaning: Urbolon bears the whale of its whale grounds.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, ink at the hoist and chart teal at the fly, by an indented line of small even teeth. A whale in chart paper, large in the centre.

countries.name: Nondondor

primary_charge.name: a short straight hanger sword
primary_charge.meaning: an isle held by the sword

marks.text: the captain's ring: the isle-lord's charge is set within a plain gold ring

countries.meaning: Nondondor, first of the corsair isles, bears the straight hanger sword within the captain's gold ring: its captain-lord holds the isle by the sword and lives by the Ransoming.
countries.blazon: A plain field of corsair black. A short straight hanger sword in bone, large in the centre. The charge is set within a plain heavy ring of bone.

countries.name: Aatah

marks.text: the captain's ring: the isle-lord's charge is set within a plain gold ring

countries.meaning: Aatah's grapnel is its boarding crews.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, corsair black above and blood red below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A grapnel in bone, large in the centre. The charge is set within a plain heavy ring of bone.

countries.name: Previous Dark

marks.text: the captain's ring: the isle-lord's charge is set within a plain gold ring

countries.meaning: Previous Dark bears the masthead lantern of the night raids it is named for.
countries.blazon: A plain field of sea ink. A masthead lantern in ransom gold, large in the centre. The charge is set within a plain heavy ring of ransom gold.

countries.name: Benan

primary_charge.name: a rope cut through
primary_charge.meaning: the hostage set free on payment

marks.text: the captain's ring: the isle-lord's charge is set within a plain gold ring

countries.meaning: Benan bears a cut rope: a hostage freed when the ransom is paid.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, blood red at the hoist and corsair black at the fly, by an indented line of small even teeth. A rope cut through in bone, large in the centre. The charge is set within a plain heavy ring of bone.

countries.name: Bono

marks.text: the captain's ring: the isle-lord's charge is set within a plain gold ring

countries.meaning: Bono's banded chest is the ransom-chest of its tide-court.
countries.blazon: A field of blood red with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of corsair black edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A banded chest in ransom gold, large in the field below the chief. The charge is set within a plain heavy ring of ransom gold.

countries.name: The Cursed Square

marks.text: the captain's ring: the isle-lord's charge is set within a plain gold ring

countries.meaning: The Cursed Square bears the moray of its hidden coves.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, corsair black above and rust below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A moray eel in bone, large in the centre. The charge is set within a plain heavy ring of bone.

countries.name: Kusu

primary_charge.name: a cormorant with wings spread to dry
primary_charge.meaning: the diver that takes and returns

marks.text: the captain's ring: the isle-lord's charge is set within a plain gold ring

countries.meaning: Kusu's cormorant drying its wings is the diver that takes and gives back.

countries.name: Tined

marks.text: the captain's ring: the isle-lord's charge is set within a plain gold ring

countries.meaning: Tined's boarding pike is its crews.

countries.name: Li

marks.text: the captain's ring: the isle-lord's charge is set within a plain gold ring

countries.meaning: Li bears an open shackle: its captives go home when the ransom comes.

marks.text: the captain's ring: the isle-lord's charge is set within a plain gold ring

countries.meaning: Lemo's barracuda is its fast raiders.
countries.blazon: A field of corsair black with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of ransom gold edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A barracuda in blood red, large in the field below the chief. The charge is set within a plain heavy ring of blood red.

countries.meaning: Arpos bears the coil of a sea-serpent: it claims the serpent waters.
countries.blazon: A field of sea ink with a pile (a broad wedge from the top edge narrowing to a point near the bottom) of blood red edged by an indented line of small even teeth. countries.name: Sondor

marks.text: the captain's ring: the isle-lord's charge is set within a plain gold ring

countries.meaning: Sondor's boarding axe is its cliff-harbour crew.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, sea ink at the hoist and rust at the fly, by an indented line of small even teeth. A boarding axe in bone, large in the centre. The charge is set within a plain heavy ring of bone.

primary_charge.meaning: the toll at the harbour mouth

marks.text: the captain's ring: the isle-lord's charge is set within a plain gold ring

countries.meaning: Cheko bears the chain across its harbour mouth, where every ship pays.
countries.blazon: A field of corsair black with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of sea ink edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A chain across a harbour mouth in ransom gold, large, standing on the base. The charge is set within a plain heavy ring of ransom gold.

countries.name: Amarelo

marks.text: the captain's ring: the isle-lord's charge is set within a plain gold ring

countries.meaning: Amarelo's spilling purse is the tribute of the chart-islands.
countries.blazon: A plain field of ransom gold. A purse spilling coins in corsair black, large in the centre. The charge is set within a plain heavy ring of corsair black.

countries.meaning: The Windy Lands bear a torn sail blown out by the wind: the stormiest of the corsair isles.

countries.meaning: Noris, the New Country, bears the well-head under the well-crown on indigo: its king is chosen by the well-lords, and water is never refused under his law.
countries.blazon: A plain field of indigo. A well-head with rope and bucket in well ochre, large in the centre. Above the charge a circlet set with small cups, in well ochre.

countries.name: Gondolin

marks.text: the well-crown: a silver circlet set with small cups

countries.meaning: Gondolin bears the shared bowl: water given and taken that made it Noris's sworn kin in the Noris Treaty.

countries.name: Vigodor
countries.meaning: Vigodor bears the wind-catcher tower of its oasis cities.

countries.name: Orato
countries.meaning: Orato bears the oryx of the open desert it rides.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, desert rose at the hoist and indigo at the fly, by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). An oryx in robe white, large in the centre.

primary_charge.name: a camel kneeling
primary_charge.meaning: the guest's camel kneels at the well

countries.meaning: The Moco bears the only camel in the arms of the East, kneeling at the well as a guest: the caravan-tribe that waters every road.
countries.blazon: A plain field of well ochre. A camel kneeling in deep indigo, large in the centre.

countries.blazon: A plain field of caravan red. A balance in bronze, outlined in linen, large in the centre.

countries.name: Drak
countries.meaning: Drak bears the hanging seal of the Stabilo Pact it signed first.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, bronze above and caravan red below, by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). A hanging wax seal in linen, large in the centre.

countries.name: Mostok
countries.meaning: Mostok's milestone is the caravan road it was built on.
countries.blazon: A field of market green with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of bronze edged by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). A milestone in linen, large in the field below the chief.

countries.name: Azano

primary_charge.name: a bronze coin stamped with a balance

countries.meaning: Azano bears the struck coin of the Pact's mint.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, linen above and market green below, by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). A bronze coin stamped with a balance in bronze, outlined in linen, large in the centre.

countries.meaning: Oreton's nested weights are its weighing halls.
countries.blazon: A field of linen with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of caravan red edged by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). Nested cup-weights in ink, large, standing on the base.

primary_charge.name: a measuring rod
primary_charge.meaning: the ell of the cloth markets

countries.meaning: Arcon bears the measuring rod of its cloth markets.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, seal wax at the hoist and colonnade stone at the fly, by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). A measuring rod in ink, outlined in linen, large in the centre.

countries.meaning: Obmi's corded bale is the caravans' load that passes its gates.

countries.meaning: Pornivior bears the counting frame of the houses' treasurers.

countries.meaning: Furro bears the toll bar across the road it taxes.
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, colonnade stone above and seal wax below, by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). A toll bar across a road in ink, outlined in linen, large in the centre.

countries.meaning: Olor's colonnade is its long market street under bronze roofs.
countries.blazon: A plain field of seal wax. A colonnade of three columns in colonnade stone, large in the centre.

primary_charge.meaning: the tall temples above the flood-line

marks.text: a narrow wavy bendlet: the king's river

countries.meaning: Alerhia, oldest of the river kingdoms, bears the temple stair under the river-diadem with its river: a priest-king above the Flood-Court.
countries.blazon: A plain field of river gold. A temple stair of seven steps in lapis, large in the centre. Behind the charge a narrow wavy diagonal band of lapis.

primary_charge.name: a river boat with a high stern

marks.text: the river-diadem: a gold collar-crown worn low
a narrow wavy bendlet: the king's river

countries.meaning: Miaed bears the high-sterned river boat: nineteen states of river trade under a king named for his river.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, river blue above and river gold below, by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). A river boat with a high stern in linen white, outlined in lapis, large in the centre. Above the charge a low collar-crown in linen white. Behind the charge a narrow wavy diagonal band of linen white.

marks.text: the river-diadem: a gold collar-crown worn low
a narrow wavy bendlet: the king's river

countries.meaning: Fosoco's kingfisher is the river it takes its king's name from.
countries.blazon: A field of reed green with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of river gold edged by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). marks.text: the river-diadem: a gold collar-crown worn low
a narrow wavy bendlet: the king's river

countries.meaning: The Delbiz Grasslands bear the bound reeds of the floodplain grass that feeds their herds.

Behind the charge a narrow wavy diagonal band of flood silt.

countries.meaning: Nara bears the stone cairn of its reef-shrine.
countries.blazon: A plain field of lagoon turquoise. A stone cairn on a reef in coral sand, large in the centre.

primary_charge.name: a thatched house on stilts
primary_charge.meaning: the stilt houses on the reef

countries.meaning: Dunn's thatched stilt house stands on its reef.

countries.name: Finn

countries.blazon: A plain field of deep reef. A conch in coral sand, large in the centre.

countries.meaning: Lua bears the cowrie of the feast shell-money.

countries.meaning: Angsutz bears its woven fish trap.

countries.meaning: Enhis Is Rond bears the nautilus of the deep water beyond its reef.

countries.meaning: Torsor bears the carved paddle of its crossings.
countries.blazon: A field of deep reef with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of coral sand edged by a wavy line (undy). A carved paddle in coral red, outlined in coral sand, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Yongrost
countries.meaning: Yongrost bears the net float of its lagoon nets.
countries.blazon: A plain field of frond green. A net float in coral sand, large in the centre.

countries.name: Meng
countries.meaning: Meng's dolphin is the companion of its boats.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, deep reef above and coral red below, by a wavy line (undy). A dolphin in coral sand, large in the centre.

countries.name: Sidea Islands
countries.meaning: The Sidea Islands bear the flying fish of the crossings between them.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, lagoon turquoise at the hoist and deep reef at the fly, by a wavy line (undy). A flying fish in coral sand, large in the centre.

countries.name: Agla

primary_charge.name: a woven sail
primary_charge.meaning: the woven sails of the island boats

countries.meaning: Agla bears the woven sail of the boats that link its three states.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, frond green above and coral sand below, by a wavy line (undy). A woven sail in deep reef, outlined in coral sand, large in the centre.

countries.name: Yumbo
countries.meaning: Yumbo bears the coral of its reef.

marks.text: a chief rayonny (the Sunhot patrons)

countries.meaning: Goodton bears the fig of the orchards that feed the sanctuaries.

countries.meaning: Guuden's water jar is the cool water given to every pilgrim at its gate.

primary_charge.meaning: the cities woven into living trees
